m.h:
The profit rate assumes 900 kills per hour. Actual profits may be higher or lower depending on speed and luck. Up to 1,200 kills per hour is possible by having a two space melee weapon with Aftershock 3.

Abyssal demons will drop a lot of sharks, which are useful for emergency food in case of low life points.

Using the Attuned ectoplasmator can make it an AFK method but at the cost of 397,440 gp per hour. To maximize profits, a BoB with super restores is an alternative way to restore prayer.

Spring cleaner is guaranteed to alchemise any items that are selected and dismantle all others, keeping the ground clean if paired with the attuned ectoplasmator or infernal urns.

Method 1

Pray Soul Split and Turmoil. Stand about four spaces east of the small pillar on the west end in the middle of the abyssal demons. Drink Aggroverload and use AoE abilities to attack the monsters. Use area loot to pick up any loot that falls to the ground.

Method 2

Same as Method 1 but pray Protect/Deflect Melee with use of a vampyrism scrimshaw/aspect and Turmoil. The scrimshaw will have an hourly cost of 4629255/3 round 0 gp.

Method 3

Pray Protect/Deflect Melee while using a Blood amulet of fury. The amulet will heal most, if not all of the damage dealt after protection prayers are added. If additional healing is needed, the Vampyrism or Penance aspect along with a healing familiar like the Bunyip and using the Devotion ability can greatly increase survivability.

Method 4

With the Death Note Relic, Infernal Ashes can be noted upon killing, which can be picked up using Area Loot. This can increase profit since Notepaper is not needed to pick up the ashes. The relic requires 108 Archaeology.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 1,300 kills per hour. Actual profits may be higher or lower depending on combat style, gear, perks, poison usage, cannon usage, Slayer task status, area competition, and luck.

Overview

Abyssal savages require 95 Slayer to damage and can be killed in the Senntisten Asylum, the Wilderness, or a player-owned dungeon after capturing souls; however, the asylum is recommended for easiest use and maximum amount of targets. They attack with magic and melee, but only use melee when the player is within melee distance. Because they are demons, demon slayer equipment and the Demon Slayer (perk) improve damage output. Use of both can add to kill speeds, increasing profitability.

Profit Strategies

The main profit from abyssal savages comes from abyssal flesh, pure essence, infernal ashes, coins, herbs, and rune salvage. Abyssal flesh is used to make abyssal armour spikes, while the noted pure essence drop makes savages useful for players who want runecrafting supplies. If killing them in the Wilderness, additional Wilderness rare drop table items such as revenant drop enhancer may also be possible.

For additional profit, use of the Scavenging perk can assist in gathering components to make things such as augmentors, equipment siphons, and liquid patch bombs.

Drop Cleaning

Using the Death Note relic notes all infernal ashes, allowing them to be collected with Area Loot. If not using Death Note, Attuned ectoplasmator can be used with a demon horn necklace to sustain prayer, though this sacrifices the ash profit.

Spring cleaner should be configured to alchemise or disassemble the rune salvage drops. This keeps the ground clean and makes area looting more reliable.

Survivability

The use of Deflect Magic, combined with Vampyrism, Enhanced Excalibur, and an Ancient elven ritual shard, should sustain health and prayer. If survivability is an issue, use Devotion in your ability rotation, and/or add the Enhanced Devoted perk to one of your augmented gear.

If health is still a problem, swapping Demon slayer gear out for magic tank gear (especially Cryptbloom armour) can make a big difference.

It is recommended players have protect melee up whenever possible. This will reduce the damage of the charge attack from ~6,000 to ~1,500. Upon entering combat the mammoths usually disable protect from melee for a few seconds. During this time Soul Split is recommended. In order to kill these efficiently players must dodge the mammoths ranged attack. When the mammoth lowers its head and grabs a rock, move two spaces while staying adjacent to the mammoth. The damage happens before the ball hits the ground, so make sure to move as soon as the mammoth lowers its trunk. Moving away will trigger a stronger special attack, so always move diagonally towards the mammoth. Occasionally it will gain a light blue bar above its head, and begin a charge attack. The recommended strategy for this attack is to tank it with the deflect melee prayer on.

A vampyrism aura is very useful.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 315 kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

There are 7 Adolescent White wolves scattered along the eastern ridge of the White Wolf Mountain in the f2p area, just north of the Taverley bank. Starting by killing the southernmost one and going north until you've killed all 7 and picked up their drops, then go back to the southern end when the first would be about to respawn. Killing all of them twice fills the inventory, then use the Lodestone Network to teleport to Taverley and bank.

However, because of the relatively slow respawn and the time needed to run back to start again, it is faster to world hop. Starting from the south, kill all 7, stay at the north end, switch to another world, then kill all 7 again from north to south, which conveniently lets you go to the bank. This can be up to 25% faster overall (depends on how fast you switch worlds) and the maximum profit per hour is based on this method.

Avoid going further north than necessary, as several aggressive level 42 wolves are found there and could be dangerous to low level players.

The profit rate assumes 450 kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Airut are level 122 monsters that can be found west of the Phoenix lair, in Mazcab, and in Kuradal's Dungeon. They require a Slayer level of 92 to kill and are killed for their bones and the level 90 Razorback gloves.

An upgraded Bonecrusher will significantly speed up kills per hour, combining it with the Death Note relic will eliminate the need to worry about the bones, as they will be sent noted to your inventory.

When fighting airut, they begin with no stat boosts, and are in a melee stance (on two feet), or ranged stance (all four). Shortly afterwards, they will increase their defensive power, making you hit less often during the fight. Occasionally, they will beat their chests; this signals their special attack. Once they start it up, they will deal inaccurate but heavy damage up to 1300 per hit for 8-10 times. This attack can be stopped with Flurry or Rapid Fire, which will stun them and damage dealt by the player is multiplied by two, allowing for an easy kill. Stuns can stop them, but if they start it when they are stunned, it will have no effect on them.

High level players can expect over 650 kills an hour while AFK on Kuradal's Dungeon standing on the south-eastern section, without the need of a Scrimshaw of vampyrism or Vampyrism aspect with the highest level melee gear and perks.

Automaton Guardians drop the rare and expensive static gloves, currently worth 15,093,496 gp, in addition to very good regular drops of herbs, seeds, and raw materials. The automatons can be accessed after completing The World Wakes and the other required quests. The easiest way to get to them is to use the Sixth-Age circuit to teleport to Guthix's Cave, and then teleporting into the main chamber by talking to the Guthixian High Druid. The guardians are located in the central part of the chamber.

The guardians are level 115 Melee-based creatures with 20,000 life points and are weak to fire spells. They have a special attack in which they pound the ground for a few seconds, dealing up to 1000 damage every other tick to any players in a two-square radius. Because they attack exclusively with melee and are located next to the entrances to the storage wings, it is quite easy to safespot them effectively, negating all damage including the special attacks.

Using Fire Surge is strongly recommended due to its low cost and high damage output, although Fire Wave is also effective. Other surge spells, while usually not 100% accurate without extreme magic potions, can still be used. Torment boosts damage by 10% and should be used if possible, although without 95 Prayer, Augury can be used from the standard prayer book. Extreme magic potions boost damage and accuracy, but super magic potions are very nearly as effective. Since you will be taking only token damage, try to use power armour like Void, Subjugation, or Virtus. Tectonic armour is not recommended due to its high usage cost. Your weapon of choice should probably be a staff since there will be a higher initial auto attack that way, although dual wielding has a better basic ability in Concentrated Blast, compared to Sonic Wave. A high level staff like the staff of light, polypore staff, Armadyl battlestaff or chaotic staff is recommended for the increased accuracy and damage.

To safespot the automatons, stand opposite one of the automatons with the entrance wall between you and the automaton as shown in the picture above. Be sure to stand at least one square behind the wall, or else the special attack may still be able to hit you depending on the placement of the automaton. Safespotting is not entirely necessary as you may be able to stun them using Impact and Asphyxiate long enough to kill them, but this is riskier and you will likely take some damage.

Unless you stand too close to the wall or don't stun one of the automatons for long enough, you shouldn't take any damage at all. With the very best equipment, each kill will take a bit less than 20 seconds — since both of the thresholds have a cooldown of 20 seconds, you can use this to your advantage and have a cycle of abilities that you use to kill the automatons. Even with lower level equipment and no prayers or potions, 30 second kills should be easy to obtain.

Attack the automaton, building up adrenaline using the basic abilities Wrack, Sonic Wave, and Combust as needed. Stun with Impact if you are not safespotting. Once you reach 50% adrenaline, use Asphyxiate, which does a great deal of damage and also re-stuns the monster. Do more basics and use the other threshold, Wild Magic, when available. If you manage to finish a kill with 100% adrenaline (and you may want to attempt this if you have high adrenaline when your target is weakened), Sunshine provides a large enough increase in damage to greatly increase your next couple of kills. Try to kill the first automaton after using this ability with only basic abilities and then immediately start the next kill with Wild Magic or Asphyxiate to quickly get in a large amount of damage before Sunshine wears off. Do more basics if needed until the automaton is dead.

Grab the drop if it's worth picking up, trying to go fast enough so your adrenaline doesn't start draining, and repeat. If you have the reflexes, try to first stun your next target with Impact, run to your drop and then cast Wrack. This will minimise time lost and will also increase damage by a small amount (as Impact will stun the automaton and Wrack does increased damage to stunned targets). If you are safespotting, run back to your safespot then immediately use another ability, or, if you are not safespotting, continue attacking as normal; the automaton will have already been stunned. The majority of the damage will probably come from the two threshold abilities, so prioritise using them immediately when they cool down if it will do full damage. Do not use Wild Magic when the automaton has less than 3,000 life points; do not use Asphyxiate when it has less than 7,000.

Armadyl's Eyrie is the south-west part of the dungeon, and requires 70 Ranged to enter. Having a piece of Armadyl-affiliated clothing is strongly recommended, or else everything in the area will be aggressive toward you.

Aviansies have relatively low life points and may be quickly killed using threshold abilities. Every third aviansie can be used to build up adrenaline in order to quickly kill the next two with threshold abilities. Doing so can result in over 300 aviansies killed per hour.

Once you run out of food or you're finished, teleport out and sell your adamant stone spirits and other items on the Grand Exchange.

m.h:
Killing black dragons gives decent combat experience as well as steady money in the form of their 100% drops, dragon bones and black dragonhide. It is recommended to use a high level ranged weapon to kill these creatures as they are weak to bolts. Two-handed or dual-wield ranged weapons may be used in conjunction with a super antifire potions to avoid dragonfire damage. A cheaper alternative with would be to use a regular antifire potion combined with protect from magic prayers, this negates damage taken highly, although food (Monkfish or better) is almost a necessity. Using an anti-dragon or dragonfire shield instead may reduce the profit. Additionally, beast of burden familiars will increase the number of kills possible between bank trips.

Consider using signs of the porter from divination to bank the dragonhides, it might boost your profit/hour due to less bank effort/more banks with the pack yak special move. Players with pack yak and Porter V will be able to kill up to 250 black dragons per hour.

One of the best places to kill black dragons is the Evil Chicken's Lair, accessed from Zanaris. This spot is rarely crowded. You need to use a raw chicken on the shrine in front of it to enter (kill one of the chickens running around the area). It's easy to bank from there, either walking to Zanaris or using a TokKul-Zo to teleport to the Fight Caves, bank, and use the fairy ring to return. If wearing a portent to the Lair, it should be noted that the portent WILL bank the raw chicken you pick up from killing one of the chickens. Unequipping the portent is necessary if obtaining a raw chicken in this manner.

Black unicorns always drop unicorn horns, worth 813 gp each. The best place to kill them is in low-level Wilderness

The unicorns are found north of Edgeville, in level 18-20 Wilderness. Walk north from Edgeville to reach them, and start attacking -- they only have 1,200 life points so they should only take a couple hits to kill, another option would be to teleport to the Wilderness Crater lodestone, which is very close to the black unicorn area. Pick up the unicorn horns, repeating until you have 28 total. The unicorns may do a small amount of damage to you unarmoured, but not enough to require food. When your inventory is full, teleport back to Edgeville using either the Edgeville lodestone or an amulet of glory, and repeat.

Black unicorn foals can often be found with Black unicorns, don't bother killing them because, despite being weaker, they will only rarely drop a Unicorn horn.

Blue dragons, found in the Taverley blue dragon resource dungeon, always drop dragon bones and blue dragonhide (along with many other chance drops), which sell for 881 and 1091 respectively. This makes each kill worth 1,972 coins.

The usage of a beast of burden such as a war tortoise allows for up to 23 kills per trip. Each trip will require about 1.5 minutes to bank hides and bones and return to the resource dungeon. The closest bank is just south of the Taverley lodestone and is very close to the entrance to the Taverley dungeon. With 70 Agility, the Agility shortcut to the blue dragon lair may be used, and running from the Taverley bank to the resource dungeon takes less than 1 minute. Banking time will approximately triple if the Agility shortcut is not used. If players find waiting for the Home Teleport too tedious, they can also use the Falador shortcut (West of the Western bank in Falador). Simply teleport with Falador Teleport tabs.

With at least 60 Dungeoneering, it is possible to enter the Taverley blue dragon resource dungeon, which is seldom crowded. Kills per hour may be maximised by picking up drops in rotation. It takes a few seconds for each dragon's drops to appear after being killed, so it is advisable to pick up the drops only after coming back to the same spot. Additionally, the number of kills per hour may be increased at level 85 Herblore by making super antifire potions, allowing the use of two-handed and dual-wield weapons.

Players with 68 Divination should consider making signs of the porter IV. Porters can send any picked up blue dragonhides to the bank, allowing you to carry more bones per trip. IV is recommend due to being among the lowest cost per item teleport (751 coins, assuming that all components are bought from the GE) and due to its 20 charge limit being comparable to a full inventory of bones plus a few miscellaneous drops. Porters will not activate on dragon bones however, but players can consider using magic notepaper on the bones or the pack-yak's winter storage special to extend their trip. Buying magic notepaper can cut into profits quite a bit, so players will have to determine whether or not the convenience is worth it to them. You may also get more kills per hour by using legacy mode, however this isn't recommended for lower combat level players.

The profit rate assumes 200 kills per hour with low input using Revolution++ while on a slayer task. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

These monsters use highly damaging ranged attacks, so it is recommended to use Protect/Deflect Missiles.

After every 6 auto attacks they gather energy from the surrounding area which draws itself towards the creature. It will then release a poison cloud dealing up to 3,000 damage in the nearby area and healing itself for 2,000 lp in the process. This attack can be avoided by running 5 squares away (Surge or Escape) or forcing the crawler to move by standing under it. The attack can also be blocked and healed in full from a well-timed Resonance.

Members of the Order of Ascension are killed for their ascension keystone drops. Capsarii are preferable to Rorarii due to their lower health, allowing for more kills per hour. Death is also extremely unlikely compared to Rorarii given their extremely low damage.

Unfortunately, compared to the other two members, Capsarii are spread fairly far apart across the dungeon. At most, there are only two areas with three spawns of Capsarii: the chamber south of Legio Primus' laboratory, and the area north of the ascended Guthix, both of which are surrounded by other members, which would make this money making method unviable.

For this reason, Capsarii souls are placed in the Sunken Pyramid for farming purposes; any room works, but the small room is the most optimal for collecting drops. The Sunken Pyramid allows the player to camp Capsarii without any competition, and provides access to five spawns. In order to access the Sunken Pyramid, the player must have 99 Slayer. If the player does not have the five Capsarii souls needed, then they can use another player's dungeon which has them as long as that person's private settings allow them to enter and both players are on the same world. However, as other players may also be using the dungeon, it's generally better to get the Capsarii souls yourself. The most ideal location to farm them is to continually sweep the south-western area of the Monastery, which contains seven fairly spaced Capsarii spawns but should be enough for any player to loop through them without world hopping.

When the Capsarii souls are collected (or if the player is using another player's dungeon), farming Capsarii is extremely simple. It is highly recommended to go into Legacy Mode while using a bow with no ammunition - such as a Zaryte bow, Decimation or Seren godbow and drink an aggression potion of any type. Legacy Mode increases the strength of your auto-attacks, and Capsarii will often die in a single hit to these weapons. Though a hexhunter bow provides a damage bonus against Capsarii, it is ill-advised due to its somewhat low damage output in Legacy Mode along with the cost of arrows. Using EoC mode allows for any ranged weapon to be used, but forces the player to pay more attention.

Augmented gear can be used with Precise 6, Eruptive 4 and Ruthless 3 will ensure 1-hitting Capsarii most of the time. Damage-increasing armour perks generally do not increase the kill rate with higher-levelled weapons, but Scavenging can be used to collect components, Enhanced efficient can be used to lower charge drain rate, or Efficient can be used to increase XP Capacitor 5000 level rate.

A steel titan is recommended to speed up kills in the event that an attack does not kill a Capsarii in a single hit; scrolls are optional. The steel titan takes higher priority over other ranged familiars, as it possesses a Ranged level of 90, and any other familiar such as a shadow nihil can miss their hit. Make sure the titan is far from Capsarii so that it does not use its melee attack; recall the titan if necessary to move it out of melee range. The titan should also focus on capsarii with low health so a player auto-attack is not wasted on them. Note that the titan may focus on another target when attempting to change its target acquisition.

Players can easily keep their health high with the Vampyrism aspect. To save on rune costs, the blood amulet of fury also helps in keeping the player's health high. An enhanced Excalibur can also be brought along for additional healing if the blood amulet is unable to keep the player's health high. Soul Split should be used if neither of these two options work, and simply flicking it ensures very little prayer points are used. If not using overloads, then standard range potions should be supplemented with the Berserker curse to slightly prolong its duration.

As little to no prayer is used, an ancient elven ritual shard may be brought along to restore any depleted prayer points.

Capsarii frequently drop various elemental battlestaves, medium adamant plated salvage and tiny spiky rune salvages, which often account for roughly 25-33% of the profit made. If a spring cleaner is taken, ensure it alchemises the aforementioned salvages, and toggle battlestaves off, as the alchemy value of the elemental battlestaff is 9,300 coins, while disassembly to base components will reduce the value of the battlestaff by almost 55%, as the spring cleaner will convert the resulting elemental orb into the respective elemental runes, cosmic runes and an unpowered orb, which yields very little money. A gold accumulator can also be taken to auto-collect coin drops, but is not mandatory. The remaining profit comes from the keystone drops. Pure essence, coal stone spirits, yew logs and unpowered orbs can be picked up but is generally not recommended as it slows kill rates.

Cave horrors drop the black mask, worth 1,484,642 gp, at a believed 1/512 rate. In addition, the vast majority of their drops are noted or otherwise stackable, allowing for long trips. They are located in the Mos Le'Harmless Caves, access to which requires completion of Cabin Fever. Players also need a light source and a witchwood icon to avoid taking a great deal of damage. The easiest ways to get to the caves are taking the fairy ring (requires A Fairy Tale III - Battle at Ork's Rift), or taking Bill Teach's boat from Port Phasmatys to Mos Le'Harmless, then travelling east from the town.

The cave horrors are a bit spread out, and they have 5,000 life points. With decent armour they don't do enough damage to be very troublesome, but a bunyip or healing abilities can be used if needed. With mid- to high-level equipment, it's very possible to kill 150.0 cave horrors per hour.

m.h:
Cave slime in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves always drop between 1 and 6 swamp tar, which is currently worth 439 coins each. The easiest way to get to the dungeon is by teleporting to Lumbridge, going into the castle basement with a light source, and enter the swamp caves by the entrance next to Mistag. Head south and west, avoiding wall beasts, until you reach an area with three cave slime. Consult Map:Lumbridge Swamp Caves for more details. Be careful of gas in the caves, as if you have an open light source (i.e. torch, oil lamp, etc.) the gas will explode dealing high damage and extinguishing your light source. A bullseye lantern or similar is recommended.

Attack the three cave slimes in the area with Magic or Ranged. At a high enough combat level you can more quickly kill them with melee. They are level 38 and only have 950 life points, so oftentimes a single hit is enough to kill them. When all three are dead, pick up the swamp tar and wait for them to respawn (it takes about ten seconds from the first one being killed). The cave slimes do use poison, but this only hits a maximum of 13 damage at a time and should not be bothered with unless you have low life points. The cave slime drop an average of 3 swamp tar per monster, and you can kill between 600-900 of them per hour at a medium combat level. This means you can collect between 1,800 and 2,700 tar per hour, depending on your combat level. Sell the swamp tar on the Grand Exchange when finished.

Celestial Dragons are commonly killed for their various noted drops, great experience, and the ease of killing them. Celestial Dragons will only attack with their dragon breath when killing them from a distance, and the damage from their dragon breath is negated completely when using Super Antifire potions, meaning defensive armour and food is not necessary.

Celestial Dragons can be assigned as a slayer task from Laniakea, Morvran, Kuradal, Lapalok, and Duradel. Killing a dragon gives 976.3 Slayer experience per kill. Whilst on a slayer task there is also a very rare chance that the dragons will drop the celestial handwraps.

Celestial Dragons can be accessed by catching the boat from the line ghost captain with his rowing boat, just north of the Port Phasmatys bank. The trip is free, arriving at the radiant wisp colony. From there, the Dragontooth Island resource dungeon is a short distance South. Players with a Hoardstalker ring or Dungeoneering cape can teleport directly to the resource dungeon.

Aside from the unique drops, dragon bones, and huge plated rune salvages, all of their drops are noted. Bones can either be noted with magic notepaper or the Death Note Archaeology relic, sent to the bank with pack yaks, or buried instantly with a bonecrusher in conjunction with a Dragon Rider amulet or demon horn necklace. If toggled, the Underworld Grimoire 3 sends dropped dragon bones directly to the focus storage; this takes priority over the bonecrusher. Alternatively, if these are not an option, dragon bones can be banked using Port Phasmatys bank.

m.t: Killing chaos dwarves and hand cannoneers
m.pg: Money making guide/Killing chaos dwarves and hand cannoneers

rq.nt: (Armadyl battlestaff, Staff of light or Abyssal wand and orb recommended)

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 520 kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

After completing Forgiveness of a Chaos Dwarf you can access the Chaos Dwarf Battlefield, filled with dwarves that drop the dragon pickaxe. It is recommended to use Magic due to the monsters' low life points, and multicombat abilities.

The dwarves and cannoneers are not very powerful, and they only have 1,000 and 2,500 life points, respectively. They get killed very quickly, so it's almost unnecessary to use threshold and ultimate abilities. However, you will want to use multicombat abilities like Chain, Dragon Breath and Tsunami, as the dwarves will crowd you and you can hit many of them at once. Sunshine can also be used to boost your damage. Try to avoid the chaos dwogres, as they will slow you down.

Try to hit the dwarves as fast as you can; the nearby Black Guard crossbowdwarfs left alive will easily decimate the chaos dwarves almost immediately. Due to attacking a chaos dwarf, nearby chaos dwarves will start to attack you. Although they do not hit very accurately, the damage will quickly stack up. To avoid this, you should have prayer restoring neck-wear like the demon horn necklace, a bonecrusher, and Soul Split to recover from your battle wounds. If you do not, you may want to use protection prayers, and occasionally use Ice Asylum or Elite Enhanced Excalibur.

With recommended stats and prayers, and effective use of multi-target abilities, you should be able to kill about 520 monsters per hour. A focused player with max stats and high level equipment (such as augmented Anima Core), Sunshine, and Soulsplit (with Bonecrusher and Twisted Bird Skull Necklace+) can expect to kill up to 1250 monsters per hour, which will result in a Pickaxe drop once every ~4 hours on average, massively increasing the profit per hour.

There are only a few drops worth picking up -- the dragon pickaxe has a drop chance of 1/5,000, so in the very long run you should get about one pickaxe per eight hours if you kill them in equal amounts. They also drop hand cannon shot, 100 at a time, which is also worth picking up as well as Muddy keys. Due to their demand in Invention, the Hand cannons dropped are also worth a good amount. Other than that, both monsters give access to the rare drop table so it is worth wearing a Ring of Wealth, even though it does not increase the chances of receiving a dragon pickaxe. Using a charming imp to pick up the charms they drop can give you about 100 gold, 40 green, 25 crimson and 20 blue charms per hour.
